curriculum.text: use developing knowledge of the meanings of words and morphemes (i.e., bases, prefixes, and suffixes) to read and spell words

parts.text: Add -ing to a base word to show it is happening now. Build each word, then read the sentences.

parts.label: Read the sentences 3 times. Colour a face each time.

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children learn the word part ing and build new words from base words, then read them in decodable sentences.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 2. Model the first one: jump + ing = jumping.
3. Children build the rest, then read each sentence.
4. Children read the page three times and colour a face each time.

parts.title: Answer key
text: Sentences: The frog is jumping. We are reading a book. The kids are playing ball.

parts.title: Ontario curriculum link (official wording)
text: B2.3 — use developing knowledge of the meanings of words and morphemes (i.e., bases, prefixes, and suffixes) to read and spell words.
In plain terms: children read and spell the everyday letter-sounds (and word parts) quickly.

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: sounding out ing part by part. Cover the rest of the word and say the target first.
Make it easier: do fewer items together first; you read, the child echoes.
Make it harder: ask the child to think of or write one more word with the target.
You'll know it worked when: the child reads the page smoothly and spots the target on sight.
